# core/set.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/set.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

A set of `u64`, built on core/hashmap.bastio.

What is proved is what the map proves: every index is in bounds, nothing
overflows, `set_len` is the number of members, and after `set_insert` the
set holds the element. A `set_contains` that says yes is a real member.
Not proved: that it says yes for every member (see core/hashmap.bastio).

`import "core/set.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/hashmap.bastio](core-hashmap.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`set_new`](#set_new) | An empty set. |
| [`set_len`](#set_len) | The number of members. |
| [`set_contains`](#set_contains) | `x` is a member. |
| [`set_insert`](#set_insert) | Adds `x`. |
| [`set_remove`](#set_remove) | Removes `x`. |
| [`set_items`](#set_items) | The members, in no particular order. |
| [`set_free`](#set_free) | Frees the set. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `HashSet`

```bastio
struct HashSet { m: HashMap[u8] }
```

Members are the keys of a map whose values carry no information.

## Functions

### `set_new`

```bastio
fn set_new() -> HashSet
  ensures set_ok(result) && result.m.len == 0
```

An empty set.

Example:

```bastio
let mut s = set_new();
assert s.m.len == 0;
let fresh = set_insert(&mut s, 7);
let again = set_insert(&mut s, 7);
let ok = fresh && !again && set_len(s) == 1 && set_contains(s, 7) && !set_contains(s, 8);
set_free(s);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `set_len`

```bastio
fn set_len(s: &HashSet) -> u64
  requires set_ok(s)
  ensures result == s.m.len
```

The number of members.

### `set_contains`

```bastio
fn set_contains(s: &HashSet, x: u64) -> bool
  requires set_ok(s)
  ensures result ==> set_has(s, x)
```

`x` is a member.

### `set_insert`

```bastio
fn set_insert(s: &mut HashSet, x: u64) -> bool
  requires set_ok(s)
  ensures set_ok(s) && set_has(s, x)
```

Adds `x`. Returns true if it was not a member before.

### `set_remove`

```bastio
fn set_remove(s: &mut HashSet, x: u64) -> bool
  requires set_ok(s)
  ensures set_ok(s)
```

Removes `x`. Returns true if it was a member.

Example:

```bastio
let mut s = set_new();
let a = set_insert(&mut s, 1);
let b = set_insert(&mut s, 2);
let had = set_remove(&mut s, 1);
let hadnt = set_remove(&mut s, 9);
let items = set_items(s);
let ok = a && b && had && !hadnt && set_len(s) == 1 && vec_len(items) == 1 && vec_get(items, 0) == 2;
vec_free(items);
set_free(s);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `set_items`

```bastio
fn set_items(s: &HashSet) -> Vec[u64]
  requires set_ok(s)
  ensures forall j: u64 :: j < vlen(result) ==> set_has(s, vget(result, j))
```

The members, in no particular order.

### `set_free`

```bastio
fn set_free(s: HashSet)
```

Frees the set.

## Specification functions

### `set_ok`

```bastio
spec fn set_ok(s: &HashSet) -> bool {
  hmap_ok[u8](s.m)
}
```

The set is well formed (what every function needs and keeps).

### `set_has`

```bastio
spec fn set_has(s: &HashSet, x: u64) -> bool {
  hmap_has[u8](s.m, x)
}
```

`x` is a member.
